Research

Science and technology development for a resilient renewable energy sector.

Research programme

Met2Adapt pioneers a disruptive and highly ambitious methodological framework that dynamically links advanced disciplines. By seamlessly cross-pollinating high-fidelity computational physics with state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning, we can rapidly model and optimize complex material behaviors. This theoretical powerhouse is firmly grounded in reality through rigorous, real-world empirical testing and continuous Structural Health Monitoring (SHM).

By streaming live data from integrated smart sensors into advanced Digital Twins—highly accurate, real-time virtual replicas of our physical infrastructure—we create a complete cyber-physical loop. This allows us to predict wear-and-tear, simulate extreme environmental stressors, and optimize performance long before an actual component degrades. Ultimately, this multidisciplinary nexus allows us to deploy highly tailored, bespoke solutions directly into the harsh, demanding environments that sustain Europe’s energy grid. By fortifying both onshore and offshore wind farms, and unlocking the immense potential of oceanic wave-energy converters, Met2Adapt is actively future-proofing the infrastructure that will define our renewable energy resilience.

Research work packages

WP1: Design

How can we engineer novel meta-material architectures with optimum vibration mitigation capabilities tailored to the specific mechanical and environmental stimuli pertinent to wind and wave energy production?

WP2: Predict

Can we derive damage indices from fast yet reliable numerical simulation fusing physics and AI?

WP3: Protect

Can we design meta-structures that are self-tuned, resilient, and adaptable to adverse environmental conditions?

View details

WP4: Sense

How can we enable a truly man-ageable and resilient green-energy production ecosystem via intelligent SHM and prognostics?

DC14João Brites

Uncertainty Quantification and Technology Qualification for Advanced Wind Turbine Components

Host: DTUSupervisors: Prof. A. Kolios, Prof. Y. Guo, Prof. J. Chiachio

Short Bio

João holds a Bachelor’s and a Master’s degree in Engineering Physics from the University of Porto. Prior to joining Met2Adapt, he completed a research internship at IFIMUP focused on sustainable energy harvesting, carried out his MSc thesis research with the CENTRA group at FEUP on space debris and satellite orbit reconstruction, and later held a research fellowship at FEUP working on astrodynamics and celestial mechanics. He is currently a Doctoral Candidate at DTU Wind and Energy Systems, focusing on uncertainty quantification and technology qualification for advanced wind turbine components.

Project summary

Develop a robust framework for uncertainty quantification (UQ) and technology qualification, aimed at validating the safety, performance, and longevity of advanced wind turbine components, particularly next-generation blades featuring adaptive meta-materials.

Methods

Baysian Inference; Stochastic modelling; performance benchmarks.

UQ Technology Qualifcation Certification

DC9Fenia Papadopoulou

Modelling of the dynamic response for offshore wind farms

Host: University of LiverpoolSupervisors: Prof. D. Colquitt, Prof. A. Movchan, Prof. A. Palermo

Short Bio

Fenia graduated with an MEng from the School of Applied Mathematical and Physical Sciences at NTUA in 2026, focusing on the mathematical modelling of wave scattering in flexural plates. Her theoretical background in PDEs, wave propagation, continuum mechanics, elasticity theory, and dynamical systems is enhanced by her practical experience using tools such as Mathematica and MATLAB. She applied this combination of skills in her thesis, “Elastic Scattering in Kirchhoff Plates” conducted under the supervision of Prof. Gourgiotis. In October 2026, she began her PhD in the Department of Mathematical Sciences, in Applied Mathematics, at the University of Liverpool, supervised by Prof. Colquitt and Prof. Movchan.

Project summary

Deliver analytical and computational models of individual and clusters of turbines, considering solid-fluid interactions, and scattering and generation of waves.

Methods

analytical modelling; nonlinear dynamics; environmental impact assessment.

DC11Braulio Neira

GenAI-aided reliability assessment of mechanical metamaterials in offshore wind and wave energy applications

Host: University of GranadaSupervisors: Prof. J. Chiachio, Prof. M.L. Jalón, Prof. A. Kolios

Short Bio

Braulio is a Mechanical Engineer specialising in renewable energy systems, with a strong focus on wave energy converters and marine energy technologies. His research combines analytical modelling, multibody dynamics, numerical simulation and experimental testing. His work has focused on the development of wave energy converters with nonlinear and variable-stiffness mechanisms, including the design and construction of lab-scale prototypes for wave-channel testing. He has gained international research experience through collaborations with RWTH Aachen University, the University of Edinburgh, the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro and other partner institutions. Braulio has contributed to journal and conference publications in marine energy and mechanical engineering, and has presented his research at international conferences, receiving recognition through a poster award.

Project summary

Develop an efficient methodological framework to quantify the structural reliability of meta-materials involving material and geometrical uncertainties.

Methods

Data augmentation; generative AI; reliability analysis.

risk machine learning wind and wave energy
